notice: Every case is PLANNED. No case has been run: no game code exists in this workspace and no browser QA was performed. Statuses must not be read as results. Corrections review applied; where this suite conflicts with ROOT_BRIEF.md, the corrections win.

cases.title: Two seats complete join, setup, play, results, rematch
cases.setup: Fresh room, minimum roster for the game.
steps: Create room and join second seat
Configure defaults and start
Play to a natural result
Rematch from results
cases.expected: Each transition lands on the correct screen with no stale snapshot content; natural completion returns results; rematch mints a new instanceId and all clients remount.
cases.evidence: Playwright snapshot assertions plus screenshots at each screen, desktop and 390px phone (phone captures are layout only).

cases.title: Host change-game and lobby-return mid-session
cases.setup: Completed match, both seats connected.
steps: Host returns room to lobby
Host configures a different game and starts it
Return to lobby again
cases.expected: Dispose runs on every teardown; no previous game audio, timers or input handlers survive; rejected lobby requests leave the current screen intact.
cases.evidence: Console log shows dispose calls; no post-teardown audio or timer callbacks in a 30s observation.

cases.title: Host End returns to lobby; leave and refresh resume by token
cases.setup: Active game with two seats.
steps: Host ends the match
One seat leaves the room
Remaining seat refreshes within the linger window and resumes by seat token
A same-name join attempts the occupied seat
cases.expected: Host End returns to lobby, never to results; disconnect/ordinary leave promises no immediate seat deletion; refresher reclaims the same seat by token under resume/grace/linger behaviour; same-name join gets a suffix instead of taking over.
cases.evidence: Authoritative lobby game:null plus native lobby return; seat identity/resume projection and duplicate-name isolation. Do not assume a new reason field in the existing lobby packet.

cases.title: Maximum-roster complete lifecycle
cases.setup: Full maximum roster for the game (8 golf, 6 rocket, 8 bomb).
steps: Fill every active seat and start
Play to a natural result
Rematch from results
Return to lobby
cases.expected: Full roster plays, results name every seat, rematch mints a new instanceId cleanly, lobby return disposes everything.
cases.evidence: Snapshots plus screenshots at each screen at desktop width.

cases.title: Ten consecutive rematches leave no residue
cases.setup: Two seats, playable build.
steps: Play and rematch ten times in a row
Observe timers, audio, input handlers and memory trend
cases.expected: Every rematch mints a fresh instanceId; no stale timers, audio, handlers or snapshot content survive; no degradation trend across the ten runs.
cases.evidence: Instance IDs, active listener/timer/render-loop/audio-node/physics-world counters plus measured heap/GPU resource trend across10rematches. Dispose logs alone do not prove memory/resource behaviour.

cases.title: Late joiner spectates until the next start
cases.setup: Game already running.
steps: Third browser joins mid-match with a room code
Current match finishes and host starts again
cases.expected: Mid-match joiner receives watch-only snapshots and their actions are dropped pre-onAction; active roster stays fixed for the match; they join play only on the next start (new instance) — for golf this means the next match, not the next hole.
cases.evidence: Server log shows dropped actions; client shows spectator chrome, then active controls after restart.

cases.title: Host disconnect migrates control without deadlock
cases.setup: Three seats, first seat is host, game in lobby.
steps: Host socket drops
A remaining player configures and starts
cases.expected: hostId migrates to longest-connected player; if no host connected, any connected player may act so the room never deadlocks.
cases.evidence: Room snapshots show new hostId; configure/start accepted from that seat.

cases.title: Active-player kick ends non-kart game to lobby
cases.setup: Small roster in play (non-kart game).
steps: Host kicks one connected active seat mid-game
Kicked client attempts to act on the old instanceId
Kicked client attempts to reclaim the seat with its old token
cases.expected: Game returns to lobby per current framework behaviour; kicked socket detached with a reason; stale-instance actions dropped; removed token cannot reclaim the kicked seat.
cases.evidence: Lobby game:null, removal reason on kicked client, stale-action rejection and failed removed-token reclaim. Do not assume an invented lobby reason field.

cases.title: Watcher kick need not end the game
cases.setup: Active match plus at least one watcher.
steps: Host kicks a watcher mid-match
cases.expected: Match continues for the active roster; watcher detached with a reason; no lobby return forced by a watcher kick.
cases.evidence: Match snapshots uninterrupted; watcher client shows removal reason.

cases.title: Rocket low-roster bounded pause/retry
cases.setup: Match in progress; drop connections until fewer than 2 connected players remain.
steps: Disconnect all but one connected player
Observe the match state
Reconnect a second player and resume
cases.expected: Below2connected players pauses repair input and saves remaining mission time. A cumulative20second reunion budget resumes with a fresh authoritative deadline/current versioned roles if met; exhaustion interrupts with Retry. No solo-success or clue leakage. Golf/Bomb have separately specified continuation policies.
cases.evidence: Interruption snapshot with reason; resume log.

cases.title: Stale instance and window guards drop old input
cases.setup: Game running; capture a valid action payload.
steps: Trigger a rematch (new instanceId)
Replay the captured payload with the old i/w values
cases.expected: Room drops the stale payload; no double-apply, no score change, no error visible to other players.
cases.evidence: Server-side drop logged; totals unchanged across the replay.

cases.title: Game-owned action sequence applies once, awaited by result
cases.setup: Game running with a non-idempotent intent available (shot, plant, toggle).
steps: Send a valid intent with sequence N
Resend the same sequence N
Send the next intent with sequence N+1
cases.expected: First applies exactly once with its result echoed in the player's private projection; resend of N never reapplies; N+1 applies normally; sequences reset with the instance; client awaited the actual sequence/result/state, not a broadcast or sleep. Idempotent operations use the simpler last-write rule.
cases.evidence: State diff shows a single application; private projection carries sequence/result.

cases.title: Old timers never fire into a new phase
cases.setup: Game with a deadline; force a phase change just before expiry.
steps: Start a short deadline
End the phase early via host
Observe past the original expiry
cases.expected: Generation-guarded timers: the stale fire is a no-op; new phase state untouched.
cases.evidence: No phase regression in snapshots after the original expiry passes.

cases.title: Simulated time tracks elapsed time at nominal and late ticks
cases.setup: Game with a 50ms tick on def.tickInterval(state); controlled clock.
steps: Run nominal ticks and compare simulated time to elapsed time
Inject late ticks forcing catch-up up to the 12-step maximum
Force debt beyond the maximum and observe the interruption policy
cases.expected: Nominal: simulated time matches elapsed (normally 3 accumulator steps per 50ms tick); late: bounded catch-up to 12 steps with retained debt; beyond-maximum: explicit excessive-lag/interruption reason, never a silent drop-then-snap; 10Hz snapshot projection stays separate throughout.
cases.evidence: Sim-time vs elapsed-time logs at nominal and late profiles; interruption reason snapshot.

cases.title: Blur, hidden tab and modal release held input
cases.setup: Active play with a held control (aim drag, stick, held key).
steps: Blur the window mid-hold
Hide the document
Open a modal over the playfield
Return
cases.expected: Captures and held keys release on blur/hidden/disposal; no stuck input; modal suspends camera/drag input; return shows a clean idle state.
cases.evidence: Manual pass on desktop plus phone rotation; no phantom movement after return.

cases.title: Background readiness distinguishes paint, resources, warm-up and suspension
cases.setup: Two clients, one tab hidden or backgrounded (release-36 Safari lesson).
steps: Start the game with one tab hidden
Observe the hidden client's readiness and the visible client's countdown
Background the tab fully and observe behaviour claims
cases.expected: Hidden client completes required resources and releases the decorative paint wait; visible client still waits for two-frame paint and first rendered frame before countdown. The run distinguishes skipped decorative paint, loaded critical resources, actual renderer warm-up and a fully suspended browser — and never claims frozen JavaScript keeps running.
cases.evidence: Readiness logs per client with the four states labelled; no match-deadline expiry caused by a hidden tab.

cases.title: 150 and 300ms RTT with jitter stay playable
cases.setup: Two clients with throttled RTT profiles (150ms, 300ms + jitter).
steps: Play a full round on each profile
Interrupt snapshot delivery for 3s mid-play
Disconnect one client for 3s and reconnect
cases.expected: Play completes; actual transport disconnect shows the shell reconnecting state and resumes by token; 3s drop does not forfeit the seat or corrupt totals. A client merely missing snapshots on an open socket is a presentation gap under the game's stale-state policy — it never invokes the shell reconnect state by itself.
cases.evidence: Throttled-network Playwright runs; snapshot continuity across the gap.

cases.title: Ties and edge-score finals read cleanly
cases.setup: Scripted finals per game: golf all hole-in-one (1 each), golf all unplayed deadline/capped (9 each under the cap-8 rule), golf equal totals, bomb equal round totals, rocket dark-ship loss.
steps: Force each scripted final
Read the results screen
cases.expected: Tied players share the rank with tie copy; every scripted final shows an honest named result, never an empty or broken board. No results copy claims a zero-stroke golf final means nobody needed a second shot.
cases.evidence: Screenshots of each results screen per game.

cases.title: Five layout states keep the playfield clear
cases.setup: One playable build per game.
steps: Render desktop, portrait phone, landscape phone, tablet, compact embed widths
Open every drawer and disclosure at the narrowest width
cases.expected: No critical ball/hazard/instrument or active control is obscured. Secondary information collapses on demand, safe-area/keyboard geometry remains usable. Record actual HUD coverage per layout rather than approve by a universal20–25percent area rule.
cases.evidence: Screenshots at all five widths per game labelled layout-only for 390px desktop captures (resized desktop proves layout, not touch); HUD-coverage estimate recorded.

cases.title: Touch-capable laptop keeps both input paths
cases.setup: Touch-capable laptop browser.
steps: Play using keyboard/mouse only
Play using touch only
cases.expected: Both paths work in the same session; touch controls appear by capability, keyboard shortcuts remain active.
cases.evidence: Physical-device pass with actual hardware evidence; cannot be proven by desktop resize.

cases.title: WebGL context loss and asset failure recover without duplication
cases.setup: Playable build with critical/optional asset manifest.
steps: Force a WebGL context loss mid-play
Block an optional asset and reload
Block a critical asset and reload
cases.expected: Context loss shows a recovery state and restores with no duplicated input or outcomes; authority may legitimately have advanced/scored while the renderer was unavailable, so unchanged score is not promised. Missing optional asset degrades dressing only; missing critical asset blocks countdown with a named reason, never a frozen frame.
cases.evidence: Forced-loss run plus blocked-request runs; countdown gating logged; no duplicate application in state diff.

cases.title: Giggle Meet panel coexists with every layout
cases.setup: Embedded room with a live call alongside play.
steps: Play one round with floating tiles (golf/bomb) and adjacent call (repairs)
Collapse and expand the media panel mid-play
cases.expected: Call never covers the active control; collapsing the panel never remounts or resets play; game opens no second capture.
cases.evidence: Live two-person Meet run with actual call evidence; embedded-mode screenshots; getUserMedia call count stays at the Meet layer only.

cases.title: First-play payload, cold start, frame budgets and thermal distribution
cases.setup: Production-shaped build on 10Mbps/100ms profile and a declared midrange phone.
steps: Measure compressed first-play bytes
Time to usable playfield with visible loading
Record p95 frame intervals on desktop and phone plus a 10-minute thermal run
cases.expected: Payload <= 4MB; playfield <= 5s; desktop p95 <= 20ms, phone p95 <= 36ms; thermal acceptance is decided by the measured 10-minute frame distribution (p95 drift, sustained throttling), not a vague no-collapse claim; local feedback <= 50ms with server ack timed separately.
cases.evidence: Measurement logs per device with the full 10-minute frame distribution; targets are proposed, results recorded as observed.

cases.title: Shared physics, network, resource and concurrent-room workload
cases.setup: Proposed declared G1 workload: four concurrent rooms, each at the target game maximum roster, defaults and busiest supported slice. Record exact server hardware/runtime, map, seed, duration and client network profile before running.
steps: Load maximum roster in one room and measure physics CPU, snapshot bytes and effect allocations
Run the declared concurrent-room count and observe cross-room interference
cases.expected: Record per-room physics/action CPU p50/p95/max, accumulator debt, snapshot cadence/bytes/traffic, entity/effect allocations and cross-room interference over10minutes. No room exceeds its declared catch-up/interruption policy; no unbounded entity/effect growth. Set measured capacity/traffic budgets before G3 approval; no unstated bounds are counted passed.
cases.evidence: Per-room workload logs under the shared load profile.

cases.title: Event audio is comfortable, ducked and disposed
cases.setup: Each game with sound on beside a call.
steps: Trigger each gameplay event sound
Dispose the view and listen for 15s
cases.expected: Sounds audible but comfortable, ducked around conversation, fully stopped on disposal; no navigation or homepage sounds exist.
cases.evidence: Heard-audio check on a physical device with actual listening evidence; post-dispose silence observed, not assumed.

cases.title: Reduced motion preserves all game information
cases.setup: prefers-reduced-motion enabled, each game mid-play.
steps: Enable reduced motion
Trigger aim, blast, repair-success and countdown states
cases.expected: No flashing/shaking; blast danger, aim direction, repair state and deadlines remain fully readable through static cues.
cases.evidence: Native short recordings/frame traces for flashing/camera motion plus still screenshots for readability; static screenshots alone do not prove absence of animation.

cases.title: Selected kit files meet the shipping bar
cases.setup: Chosen per-file shortlist from the three Kenney kits plus original meshes.
steps: Record source URL and CC0 license per file
Check units, pivots, materials and collision proxies
Measure compressed bytes, decode cost and mobile LOD behaviour
cases.expected: Every shipped file has a license line; consistent units/pivots; explicit proxies where physics touches; critical vs optional manifests honoured; no runtime primitive model-building during attacks.
cases.evidence: Asset ledger with per-file rows; measurement logs.

cases.title: Rest needs contact, low velocities and stable drift
cases.setup: Balls rolling near rest on flat, uphill and sloped lies; server step logs visible.
steps: Roll balls at just above and just below the tuned envelope
Rest a ball on a slope and watch for creep
Attempt a second shot during roll and after rest
cases.expected: Rest requires supported contact plus low linear velocity, low angular velocity and stable positional drift over the hold window, all relative to final model units and ball radius; a visibly creeping sloped ball never reads as ready. Rolling balls reject with 'ball rolling', never queue; renderer prediction never overrides the server verdict. No fixed velocity number is asserted as release fact before G1 tuning.
cases.evidence: Server step logs vs client presentation; sloped-ball creep run; second-shot-during-roll rejected in snapshots.

cases.title: Cup capture uses geometry, contact and sweep semantics
cases.setup: Balls aimed at the cup across the speed range, including rim-line and high-speed lines.
steps: Putt hot at the cup
Putt soft at the cup
Roll a ball across the cup mouth at capture-boundary speed
cases.expected: Capture follows the stated capture volume, contact arc and per-step sweep (no tunnelling); balls outside the tuned envelope lip out with a visible rim bounce and stay live; soft balls drop. Both outcomes come from the server under a centre-speed predicate plus geometry, never the predicate alone.
cases.evidence: Native short recording/frame trace of cup contact, authoritative contact/capture log and selected screenshots; static screenshots alone do not prove bounce timing.

cases.title: Eighth putt, deadline grace and early settle end a hole fairly
cases.setup: Player at 7 strokes; hole deadline near expiry; ball near the edge; one ball rolling at deadline.
steps: Hole out on the 8th stroke
Leave another ball unholed after its 8th stroke settles
Let the deadline expire mid-roll for a third player
Knock a ball out of bounds
Settle every roster ball and watch the hole end
Take stroke7 out of bounds so its penalty consumes the eighth score slot; attempt another shot
cases.expected: An eighth accepted putt resolves before capping: holed records8, otherwise settled/reset unholed caps9. Penalties consume the same budget: stroke7 plus OB reaches8 unholed, caps9 with no extra shot. Capped score clamps9. Receipt time closes new shots at deadline; prior rolling balls get bounded4second grace, same-step cup capture counts, remaining unholed balls cap9. All-settled early finish names its goal reason.
cases.evidence: Recap snapshots show correct strokes and reasons per ball; grace indicator screenshot (single indicator, no second timer).

cases.title: Eight simultaneous balls stay readable and independent
cases.setup: Full 8-seat room on Banker's Garden.
steps: All players putt within the same second
One player aims while seven balls roll
cases.expected: No physical interaction between balls; every ball identifiable by pattern + colour; aiming player sees no crowd occlusion; camera stays stable while aiming.
cases.evidence: 8-client screenshot during mass putt; aim-drift measurement while others roll.

cases.title: Early finisher spectates without affecting play
cases.setup: One player holes out while others still putt.
steps: Holed player follows a friend's ball
Holed player attempts shot input
A new browser joins mid-match
cases.expected: Follow is view-only; any shot input from a holed player is rejected; remaining players unaffected. The mid-match joiner stays a spectator until the next start (new instance), not the next hole.
cases.evidence: Snapshot shows follow target change with no state mutation; joiner client shows spectator chrome.

cases.title: Aim gesture cancels safely by drag-back and Esc
cases.setup: Ball at rest, aiming.
steps: Drag out then drag back to the ball and release
Aim and press Esc
Release outside the arena
cases.expected: All three cancel with zero strokes charged and the ball undisturbed; specified cancel semantics, no accidental putts.
cases.evidence: Stroke count unchanged across all three cancels on desktop and touch.

cases.title: Shot intent carries the player sequence and awaits its result
cases.setup: Ball at rest; capture the shot payload.
steps: Putt with sequence N and read the private projection
Resend sequence N
Putt again with N+1 after rest
cases.expected: First putt applies once with stroke/result echoed for that player; resend of N never re-applies; client awaited the actual sequence/result/state, not a broadcast or sleep.
cases.evidence: Stroke diff shows a single application; private projection carries sequence/result.

cases.title: First-time player putts within 20 seconds and names the bank
cases.setup: Greybox Banker's Garden, first-time player, no coaching.
steps: Open the hole
Observe time to first putt
Ask what the risky route is after two holes
cases.expected: First putt inside 20s; player can describe the bank option; misunderstandings recorded verbatim; voluntary rematch or not recorded without pressure.
cases.evidence: Human-gate notes: timings, quotes, rematch choice.

cases.title: Both screens carry useful complementary information with necessary controls
cases.setup: Teaching attempt; per-seat views and action logs instrumented.
steps: Play the attempt with each seat's information isolated in turn
Attempt the attempt from a single seat using both sheets read aloud
Complete the attempt with full crew communication
cases.expected: Each seat's private information proves useful and complementary; each role's distinct controls prove necessary (log shows the effect each seat alone cannot produce); reading both sheets aloud is legitimate cooperation and allowed to succeed; success requires observed communication, not a message-per-link rate.
cases.evidence: Per-seat view diffs plus action logs; completed-attempt transcript showing the exchange.

cases.title: Every crew size gives everyone owned work with a first-minute action
cases.setup: Crews of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 on the timed rescue.
steps: Play the rescue at each crew size
Ask each player what they owned and what they did first
cases.expected: 2 bundles three atoms each, 3 pairs two each, 4-5 combine useful groups, 6 gives one atom each; every player names a decision only they made and a concrete first-minute action; nobody reports holding scraps of text without a control. Order uses a seed-private startup constraint and necessary target choice, not a known public lights/pumps/engine sequence. Six-player engagement remains a human hypothesis.
cases.evidence: Post-mission ownership interviews plus action log per seat at each crew size.

cases.title: Text and pings alone complete the mission at parity
cases.setup: Voice muted for the whole crew.
steps: Complete the teaching attempt using only text and the ping palette
Time it against a voice crew baseline
cases.expected: Mission completes; no voice-only information exists; ping palette covers confirm/deny/rhythm/legend requests.
cases.evidence: Text-only transcript of a completed mission; parity checklist vs voice run.

cases.title: Physical keyboard-open phone completes a text-only timed rescue
cases.setup: Physical phone with software keyboard open; timed rescue; voice muted.
steps: Play the timed rescue text-only on the phone
Keep the current clue/control visible and send actions with the keyboard open
cases.expected: Keyboard-open layout retains the current clue/control and the send action stays reachable; mission completes on text alone.
cases.evidence: Physical-device pass with actual hardware evidence; screenshots of the keyboard-open layout mid-mission.

cases.title: Wrong breakers forgive; expiry loses cleanly with rotation
cases.setup: Teaching attempt, then timed rescue.
steps: Throw two wrong breakers
Let the timed rescue expire with systems dark
cases.expected: Amber flash + buzz, no score damage, one bounded hint offered; expiry shows 'Ship cold. Retry?' with role rotation offered.
cases.evidence: Screenshots of feedback and loss screens; hint text bounded to the mission.

cases.title: Role reassignment is atomic, versioned and bounded
cases.setup: Four-player rescue; role versions instrumented.
steps: Disconnect a role owner mid-mission
Observe reassignment
Act with the old owner's client and an old version number
cases.expected: Transfer is atomic with a role version and stays with the new owner until an explicit safe reassignment boundary; old owner/version actions are rejected; with fewer than 2 connected players the mission pauses under the named interruption policy with retry — no leaked private clues, no solo-finish pretence. Cancel a transferring role's pending candidate before atomic transfer; approvals tied to a link revision are invalidated by changed cable/rhythm/route/feed/bus/target. Old owner/version and old certification cannot authorize changed state.
cases.evidence: Per-seat view() diffs proving no leak; rejection log for old-version actions; interruption snapshot.

cases.title: Reconnect reclaims the current role, never a parallel old control
cases.setup: Role transferred after a disconnect; owner reconnects by seat token.
steps: Reconnect the original owner by seat token
Attempt to act on the pre-disconnect control
cases.expected: Reconnect receives the currently assigned responsibilities; the old control cannot be restored in parallel; pre-transfer actions are rejected by version.
cases.evidence: Reconnect snapshot shows current assignment; parallel-control attempt rejected in logs.

cases.title: First-time text-only crew finishes teaching in 6 minutes
cases.setup: Two first-time players, voice muted, no coaching.
steps: Start the teaching attempt
Record misunderstandings, engagement and completion time
cases.expected: Completion within 6 minutes; notes record misunderstandings, observed communication, role engagement and whether the crew voluntarily continues; screenshot-sharing or reading sheets aloud is logged as cooperation, never as failure.
cases.evidence: Human-gate notes with timings and quotes.

cases.title: Movement, occupancy, order, fuse, blast and capacity behave exactly
cases.setup: Scripted arena: wall, cover, two bombs in line; 50ms tick logs visible.
steps: Step into a cell as another character steps into the same cell
Plant while moving into an occupied cell
Plant and time the fuse
Detonate with cover in an arm path
Plant twice in quick succession
cases.expected: Proposed200ms cardinal movement commits destination on accepted step; characters overlap and never reserve/block either cell. Walls/cover/bombs block entry; move resolves before plant at committed cell. Proposed2.5second fuse, three-cell arms, one live bomb per player, one-second cooldown. One immutable start-step obstacle snapshot governs the entire recursively expanded due/chain batch; union destruction/deaths commits once.
cases.evidence: Tick-level server log matched to rendered frames.

cases.title: Planter re-entry, simultaneous deaths and vulnerable disconnect
cases.setup: Arena with planted bombs and scripted final exchanges.
steps: Planter leaves then re-enters their bomb cell
Kill the last two players in the same commit
Disconnect a living player mid-round and blast their cell
Walk two characters through each other
cases.expected: Bomb-cell re-entry fails after leaving; same-batch final deaths draw. Connected/disconnected characters never body-block. Away players remain vulnerable and fuses continue; reconnect resumes true state. A game-owned10second continuous-away timeout forfeits round eligibility without deleting room/token. Away players cannot take a survivor win; zero-connected10seconds interrupts without a winner, independently of wholly-empty-room cleanup.
cases.evidence: Server occupancy and commit logs; draw verdict screenshot; reconnect-state snapshot.

cases.title: Spawns prove a reachable safe destination; sweeps are sample coverage
cases.setup: Generator with runtime validation; seed sweep harness.
steps: Generate arenas and inspect validation verdicts
Run a finite seed sweep
Attempt to start a rejected layout
cases.expected: Every accepted spawn proves a reachable safe destination outside the projected blast using actual movement speed, obstacles, turn/plant occupancy and fuse time; unsafe layouts are rejected before play. The finite sweep is reported as sample coverage with its seed count, never as proof over every seed.
cases.evidence: Validation log per spawn; sweep report stating seed count and sample status; rejection before play.

cases.title: Three fixed rounds, draws, and deadline blast precedence
cases.setup: Match at one round each with the third round scripted: two survivors at deadline plus one bomb due exactly at expiry.
steps: Play three fixed 45s rounds
Hold two survivors to the deadline with a due detonation pending
Submit an input after the deadline
Keep an active lingering flame at the deadline and trigger a due bomb that chains into another; inspect terminal settlement
cases.expected: Exactly three rounds with45second maximum each; complete chain batch can end a round early. Deadline applies active flame hazards plus every due/recursive detonation before deciding; later input/fuses excluded. Lingering FX after terminal verdict are visual only. Multiple/zero survivors draw; a single eligible connected survivor wins; most round wins takes match and equal totals tie.
cases.evidence: Round/match verdict snapshots; commit log showing due-blast resolution order.

cases.title: Chain ordering follows the authoritative bomb sequence
cases.setup: Three bombs where one blast catches two others with cover between them.
steps: Plant the scripted chain
Detonate the first bomb
cases.expected: A unique server-global bomb ID orders cross-player bombs. Recursively expand all triggered bombs once against the same start-step wall/cover snapshot before any destruction/death commit. Combined destruction/deaths commit once. Traversal/array order does not change outcomes.
cases.evidence: Commit log with bomb-sequence ordering; frame-matched blast rendering.

cases.title: One avatar, bounded prediction, measured corrections
cases.setup: 300ms RTT client near a live blast; correction logging on.
steps: Move out of a blast line at the last moment
Plant on an occupied cell
Multi-touch move plus plant together
Drop snapshots on the open socket without disconnecting transport
cases.expected: One readable avatar, no predicted twin; prediction is bounded and visually distinct from confirmed state with consistent presentation time for remote actors/hazards; rejections name their reason with replayable outcomes; correction frequency/distance logged and normal latency causes no misleading deaths. Interpolation states its delay buffer, bounded extrapolation and stale-state policy; open-socket snapshot gaps never invoke the shell reconnect state.
cases.evidence: Correction frequency/distance log; side-by-side prediction/confirmed rendering check; plant-reject copy screenshot.

cases.title: Blocked UI, modal and blur cannot strand or misfire input
cases.setup: Round in progress.
steps: Plant with a modal open
Blur mid-move
Rotate the phone mid-round
cases.expected: Blocked/modal input is refused with feedback, never silently applied; blur and rotation cancel gestures; no bomb plants from a cancelled orbit or pinch.
cases.evidence: Device pass; input log shows cancels, not ghost plants.

cases.title: Deaths read fairly, waiting stays short, rematches are voluntary
cases.setup: Four-player greybox arena, first-time players.
steps: Play three rounds
Ask each eliminated player why they died
Time eliminated-player waits and count rematches
cases.expected: Notes collect misunderstandings, disputed deaths, observed fairness/waiting and voluntary rematches; an unexplained replay/UI-authority disagreement blocks advancement while ordinary competitive disappointment is not a defect; unanimous 'my fault' is not required; any misleading rendered escape fails the input-presentation contract.
cases.evidence: Human-gate notes: death quotes, wait timings, rematch rate.

cases.title: Away forfeiture cannot obstruct wins or farm solo rounds
cases.setup: Three-player match; disconnect two players long enough to trigger game-owned away forfeiture.
steps: Apply10second away forfeiture and inspect survivor counting
Finish the current round with the remaining eligible survivor
Keep only one connected roster seat at the next-round boundary
Reconnect another roster member before the20second wait, then repeat with no rejoin
cases.expected: Forfeited players are excluded from survivor count and cannot block early win. A new round needs at least2connected roster players. Rejoin inside20seconds starts a real next round; otherwise incomplete match interrupts without extra solo round awards or a completed three-round champion. Room tokens are not revoked by this game policy.
cases.evidence: Authoritative eligibility/round state and native waiting/interruption views; no invented per-seat platform grace expiry.

rootNormalization: Parent incorporated independent revision2 corrections; DESIGN_SPEC.md is authoritative. All cases remain planned, with no execution evidence.
